---
title: Quick Start
---

This guide creates one generic S3-compatible backup from a source checkout.

## 1. Install

```sh
make install-deps
make install
```

`make install-deps` installs the required Homebrew tools. `make install` creates
the uv environment.

## 2. Configure a repository

Copy the commented template:

```sh
cp config.template.yaml config.yaml
```

Edit its first credential, store, and backup entries. For a generic backup:

- replace every `CHANGE_ME` used by the enabled store;
- set the store endpoint, region, bucket, and `key_prefix`;
- give the backup a useful ID such as `documents`;
- make its `restic-store-id` match the enabled store ID;
- delete unused example entries if desired.

Keep the repository password safe: restic cannot decrypt snapshots without it.

Set the config path once for the shell and validate it:

```sh
export RESTIC_BACKUPS_CONFIG="$PWD/config.yaml"
uv run restic-backups check-config
uv run restic-backups generic list
```

## 3. Initialize and back up

Initialize a new repository once:

```sh
uv run restic-backups generic init
```

Then back up any local path. Replace `documents` with your backup ID:

```sh
uv run restic-backups generic run --backup documents backup "$HOME/Documents"
uv run restic-backups generic run --backup documents snapshots
```

Existing restic repositories do not need `generic init`.

## 4. Verify a restore

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/restic-restore-check
uv run restic-backups generic run --backup documents \
  restore latest --target /tmp/restic-restore-check
```

Inspect the restored files before relying on the backup. Continue with
[Generic Backups](generic.qmd) for repository commands or
[Voice Memos Backups](voice-memos.qmd) for the macOS workflow.

::: {.callout-warning}
Do not commit `config.yaml`, credentials, repository passwords, or restored
data. Use [SOPS configuration](configuration.qmd) before committing a config.
:::
